hero.title: Named in the Gazette
hero.subtitle: Issue 156 names برجیس صاحب for a khilʿat; issue ~219 grants sick leave to England — the journey that never finished

media.alt: Engraving of the royal audience chamber in Tehran — the world of ministers and court news Edward Burgess served
media.caption: Audience chamber, Tehran — Benjamin, 1887 (period context)

media.alt: Lithographed masthead of Vaqāye-e Ettefāqiye issue 131, 28 Shawwāl 1269 AH
media.caption: Issue 131, 4 August 1853 — ناخوشی and flight from the city on the same opening page

media.alt: Newspaper scan: London Evening Standard, 17 December 1853, Persia column naming Mr Burgess and his fever
media.caption: London Evening Standard, 17 December 1853 — Tehran dispatch of 30 October

media.alt: Lithograph page naming برجیس صاحب and the royal khilʿat of Kashmiri shawl
media.caption: NLIR vol. 2, PDF p. 186 — issue 156 court notice (transcription in corpus)

media.alt: Mid-nineteenth-century Kashmiri shawl with central medallion and large boteh motifs — the kind of luxury textile given as court khilʿat
media.caption: Moon shawl with boteh motifs — typical luxury grade for court khilʿat (reference photo)

media.alt: Masthead of issue 156: Thursday 28 Rabīʿ al-Thānī 1270 AH
media.caption: Issue 156 masthead — dated late January 1854 (25 issues after no. 131)

media.alt: Portrait of Henry Burgess — Edward’s father, to whom he wrote that leave was not secure until published in the Gazette
media.caption: Henry Burgess — Edward’s 26 February 1855 letter awaited formal notice in the state paper

media.alt: Lithograph court bulletins naming Burgess Ṣāḥeb and granting sick leave to England and London
media.caption: NLIR vol. 2, PDF p. 581 — ~issue 219: اذن مریض, dispatch to England (corpus translation)

media.alt: Eugène Flandin lithograph panorama of Tabriz — the city where Edward Burgess died on the road from Tehran
media.caption: Tabriz, 1840s (Flandin) — Edward reached his old home city but not England
